dataset_info.description: Extracted abdominal and pelvic incidental findings guideline definitions from ACR white papers for dataset engine mapping

findings.description: An ovarian or paraovarian cyst identified incidentally on CT or MRI in a nonpregnant postmenarchal patient with no known adnexal disorder.
features: Oval or round shape [cite: 1932]
Unilocular mass of uniform fluid signal and attenuation [cite: 1932]
Regular or imperceptible wall [cite: 1932]
Absence of solid areas or mural nodules [cite: 1932]
Maximum diameter is strictly less than 10 cm [cite: 1932]
May contain layering hemorrhage if the patient is premenopausal [cite: 1933]

findings.description: An adnexal cyst that would otherwise meet all criteria for a benign-appearing cyst but fails on specific imaging or technical parameters.
features: Displays angulated margins [cite: 1938]
Is not round or oval in shape [cite: 1938]
A portion of the cyst is poorly imaged, such as being obscured by metal streak artifact [cite: 1938]
Image demonstrates reduced signal-to-noise ratio, often due to technical parameters or lack of intravenous contrast [cite: 1938, 1939]

findings.description: An adnexal mass displaying complex features that place it outside of benign or probably benign cyst definitions.
features: Presence of a solid component [cite: 2005]
Presence of a mural nodule [cite: 2005]
Presence of septations [cite: 2005]
Demonstrates higher than fluid attenuation [cite: 2005]
Contains layering hemorrhage if found in a postmenopausal patient [cite: 2005]

findings.description: A specific characteristic adnexal mass with known potential for malignant transformation.
features: No specific features identified on CT [cite: 2077]
Displays hyperintense T1 signal intensity and T2 shading on MRI [cite: 2077]
Often exhibits multiplicity or other pelvic findings of endometriosis [cite: 2077]
Carries a known small risk for the development of clear cell carcinoma [cite: 2068]
Merits long-term surveillance even if entirely asymptomatic [cite: 2069]

findings.description: A benign ovarian neoplasm containing characteristic mature tissue elements.
features: Ovarian mass containing visible fat or macroscopic lipid [cite: 2077]
May contain a well-defined tooth or focal calcium, which is better detected on CT [cite: 2077]
Known to enlarge slowly over time [cite: 2073]
Carries approximately a 1% risk for malignant transformation, which typically presents in uniformly very large lesions [cite: 2074, 2078]

findings.description: A progressive, permanent increase in the luminal diameter of the abdominal aorta.
features: Categorized by relationship to renal arteries as suprarenal (normal up to 3.0 cm) or infrarenal (normal up to 2.0 cm) [cite: 2193, 2194]
Defined as an infrarenal aortic diameter greater than or equal to 3.0 cm or dilation greater than or equal to 1.5 times normal [cite: 2195]
Strong association exists between initial size and subsequent expansion rate [cite: 2198]
Rupture risk increases drastically as the aneurysm diameter exceeds 5.0 cm [cite: 2200]
Follow-up is considered unnecessary if the diameter is strictly less than 2.5 cm [cite: 2207, 2213]

findings.description: Disruption of an atherosclerotic plaque leading to the penetration of luminal blood into or through the aortic wall.
features: Presents as a localized plaque disruption that penetrates variable distances into the wall [cite: 2217]
Typically encountered in elderly patients with advanced generalized atherosclerosis [cite: 2220]
May look similar to saccular pseudoaneurysms or small true aneurysms on cross-sectional imaging [cite: 2221]
Natural history is unpredictable; can progress to an intramural hematoma, focal dissection, pseudoaneurysm, or complete rupture [cite: 2219, 2222]
Absence of clinical symptoms does not imply structural stability [cite: 2223]

findings.description: Aneurysmal dilatation of the common, internal, or external iliac arteries.
features: Defined as an iliac vessel diameter greater than or equal to 2.5 cm or greater than or equal to 1.5 times the normal diameter [cite: 2226]
Involves the common and internal iliac arteries significantly more often than the external iliac arteries [cite: 2225]
Lesions strictly less than 3.0 cm expand slowly, are typically asymptomatic, and rarely rupture [cite: 2228]
Lesions greater than 3.5 cm exhibit a significantly greater tendency to rupture [cite: 2232]

findings.description: The most common type of visceral artery aneurysm found within the abdomen.
features: The vast majority are true aneurysms, though rare pseudoaneurysms can form in the setting of acute or chronic pancreatitis [cite: 2236, 2241]
Spontaneous rupture is rare for lesions measuring less than 2.0 cm [cite: 2243]
Risk factors for rupture include rapidly increasing size, occurrence in women of childbearing years, or presence of cirrhosis [cite: 2244]
Surveillance growth data demonstrates a mean expansion rate of approximately 0.06 cm per year [cite: 2247]
Surgical/endovascular treatment threshold is widely established at a diameter greater than or equal to 2.0 cm [cite: 2245]

findings.description: An uncommon aneurysmal dilation of the renal arterial tree.
features: Etiologies include fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), advanced atherosclerosis, or parenchymal pseudoaneurysms secondary to trauma [cite: 2252, 2257]
FMD-related aneurysms exhibit a characteristic 'string of beads' pattern, commonly in younger women with hypertension [cite: 2256]
Non-FMD aneurysms typically locate at major arterial branch points [cite: 2258]
Lesions measuring between 1.0 cm and 1.5 cm are considered safe for conservative observation [cite: 2261]
Surgical or endovascular intervention is recommended for stable lesions exceeding 1.5 cm to 2.0 cm, or if greater than or equal to 1.0 cm with uncontrolled hypertension [cite: 2260, 2264]

findings.description: A rare visceral artery aneurysm carrying an elevated systemic risk profile.
features: Involves the pancreaticoduodenal arterial arcade [cite: 2391]
Considered to be at a substantially higher baseline risk for spontaneous rupture regardless of size [cite: 2275]
Consensus dictates consideration for prompt surgical or endovascular treatment immediately upon detection, bypassing standard size thresholds [cite: 2275, 2236]

findings.description: A dissection limited strictly to a single visceral arterial branch, most commonly the superior mesenteric artery (SMA).
features: Most frequently involves the superior mesenteric artery [cite: 2280]
Can be encountered completely incidentally in asymptomatic individuals [cite: 2280, 2281]
Natural history under conservative management shows high rates of non-progression, improvement, or complete spontaneous resolution [cite: 2281, 2282]

findings.description: An anatomic variant involving the extrinsic compression of the pelvic venous system.
features: Anatomically defined as compression of the left common iliac vein by the crossing right common iliac artery [cite: 2299]
Present as an asymptomatic variant in up to 25% of the general population [cite: 2300]
Follow-up is explicitly unnecessary unless the patient develops specific unilateral lower-extremity symptoms, such as left-sided leg swelling or deep venous thrombosis [cite: 2299, 2300]

findings.description: An anatomic vascular compression variant involving the left renal vein.
features: Anatomically characterized by compression of the left renal vein between the abdominal aorta and the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) [cite: 2301]
Often presents with localized varices or early retrograde opacification of the gonadal venous system [cite: 2301, 2326]
Considered a clinically unimportant 'leave-alone' finding in the absence of documented flank pain, hypertension, proteinuria, or hematuria [cite: 2301, 2302]

findings.description: Thrombus formation discovered incidentally within the abdominal or pelvic venous structures.
features: Direct or indirect imaging signs differentiate acute thrombus (low attenuation, peripheral mural enhancement) from chronic configurations [cite: 2305, 2328]
Chronic thrombosis is explicitly characterized by a small, contracted vein, wall thickening, presence of intraluminal webs, or extensive regional collateral vessels [cite: 2313, 2329]
Once meeting the criteria for a chronic thrombosis, follow-up imaging is not recommended [cite: 2313]

findings.description: Incompetence and marked dilatation of the ovarian or pelvic venous plexuses.
features: Ovarian vein diameter exceeding a threshold of 8 mm [cite: 2318]
Highly common, routine incidental finding in completely asymptomatic multiparous women [cite: 2318, 2322]
Can present with extreme tortuosity and parauterine dilation (mean diameter 5.9 mm) without causing symptoms [cite: 2325]
No further imaging or intervention is recommended if the finding is asymptomatic [cite: 2323]

findings.description: A benign, fluid-filled primary or secondary space-occupying lesion of the spleen.
features: Characterized on CT by a sharply defined, well-circumscribed, low-attenuation lesion [cite: 2525]
Demonstrates near-water attenuation values strictly less than 10 Hounsfield Units (HU) [cite: 2491]
Wall is thin, smooth, or completely imperceptible, displaying no internal contrast enhancement [cite: 2491, 2525]
On MRI, demonstrates uniform low signal on T1-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images (equal to CSF) without internal nodules [cite: 2526, 2527]
Thick, dense peripheral wall calcifications (exceeding 5 mm) represent old hematomas or post-traumatic cysts and are confidently benign [cite: 2528, 2529]

findings.description: The most common primary benign vascular neoplasm affecting the splenic parenchyma.
features: Hypoattenuating on unenhanced CT, iso- to hypointense on T1 MRI, and hyperintense on T2 MRI sequences [cite: 2533]
Exhibits variable, prolonged contrast enhancement on delayed phases due to slow internal blood filling [cite: 2532, 2533]
Crucially lacks the typical crisp, discontinuous, peripheral centripetal 'flash-filling' enhancement pattern classic to hepatic hemangiomas [cite: 2491, 2532]

findings.description: A rare, benign primary solid tumor of the spleen composed of anomalous mixtures of normal tissue elements.
features: Appears isoattenuating or slightly hypoattenuating relative to normal spleen on unenhanced CT scans [cite: 2535]
Characteristically hyperintense relative to normal adjacent splenic tissue on T2-weighted MRI pulse sequences [cite: 2535]
Demonstrates early heterogeneous contrast enhancement post-injection, which fades into prolonged, uniform enhancement on delayed imaging [cite: 2536]

findings.description: A benign vascular malformation of the lymphatic system within the spleen, often mimicking metastatic disease.
features: Presents as a single or multicystic, sharply marginated space-occupying mass [cite: 2537, 2540]
Frequently occupies a distinctly subcapsular location [cite: 2515, 2540]
Displays low signal on T1 MRI and uniform high signal intensity on T2 MRI pulse sequences [cite: 2513]
Components may occasionally show high T1 signal intensity due to proteinaceous or hemorrhagic internal content [cite: 2539]
Exhibits zero internal contrast enhancement on post-contrast evaluation phases [cite: 2513, 2540]

findings.description: An indeterminate solid or complex splenic mass demonstrating criteria highly suspicious for primary malignancy (angiosarcoma) or metastasis.
features: Demonstrates marked structural heterogeneity on unenhanced or post-contrast phases [cite: 2491, 2510]
Features poorly defined, irregular, or distinctly infiltrating structural margins [cite: 2491, 2510]
Presence of central tissue necrosis, splenic parenchymal distortion, or direct vascular invasion [cite: 2491]
Associated with multiplicity of solid lesions or progressive substantial structural enlargement over time [cite: 2491, 2510]

findings.description: An incidentally identified lymph node in the abdomen or pelvis that meets quantitative or qualitative criteria for structural abnormality.
features: Short-axis diameter is greater than or equal to 1.0 cm when located within the retroperitoneal space [cite: 2572, 2597]
Morphological loss of normal elongated architecture, transforming into a round configuration with an obscured or indistinct fatty hilum [cite: 2572, 2601]
Demonstrates abnormal enhancement patterns, such as internal central necrosis or profound hypervascularity [cite: 2572, 2603]

Meets numeric clustering criteria: a cluster of greater than or equal to 3 lymph nodes within a single nodal station, or a cluster of greater than or equal to 2 lymph nodes spanning greater than or equal to 2 distinct anatomical regions [cite: 2572, 2609]

findings.description: A common, benign fibroinflammatory condition affecting the mesenteric fat that frequently coexists with or mimics adenopathy.
features: Characterized by encapsulated infiltration of the abdominal mesenteric fat [cite: 2633]
Exhibits a pathognomonic 'fat halo sign'—a preserved, completely normal rim of fat immediately surrounding adjacent mesenteric vessels [cite: 2633]
The presence of the fat halo sign serves to actively differentiate it from metastatic adenopathy, lymphoma, or desmoid tumors [cite: 2633]

findings.description: A mucosal projection into the gallbladder lumen, discovered incidentally on cross-sectional imaging.
features: Presents as a small, non-shadowing focal soft-tissue project from the gallbladder wall into the lumen [cite: 2734]
Malignancy is exceedingly rare in small lesions; size is the dominant risk stratifier [cite: 2781]
Polyps measuring less than or equal to 6 mm demonstrate negligible risk and require no further action [cite: 2734, 2777]
Polyps measuring 7 mm to 9 mm carry a minor risk of adenoma/early cancer and warrant sequential monitoring [cite: 2734, 2776]
Polyps measuring greater than or equal to 10 mm carry an elevated risk profile, especially if accompanied by demonstrable documentable growth [cite: 2734, 2779]

findings.description: Calcification within the gallbladder wall, ranging from focal segments to a completely calcified structure.
features: Exhibits focal or diffuse calcification localized within the structural wall layers [cite: 2734]
Diffuse mural calcification is traditionally termed 'porcelain gallbladder' [cite: 2734, 2747]
True baseline association with gallbladder carcinoma in modern surgical series is 5% to 7%, rather than older historic highs [cite: 2747]
Risk is highest (up to 7%) in cases with partial, focal mucosal calcification, rather than uniform diffuse calcification [cite: 2750, 2752]

findings.description: Generalized, symmetric thickening of the gallbladder wall measuring greater than 3 mm without an associated soft-tissue mass.
features: Demonstrates a measurement greater than 3 mm in wall thickness that is uniform or near-uniform globally [cite: 2734, 2766]
Frequently caused by secondary extrinsic medical conditions (e.g., hepatitis, acute/chronic liver disease, congestive heart failure, pancreatitis, or hypoproteinemia) [cite: 2734, 2767]
In the absence of a distinct focal nodule or asymmetric mass, the risk of underlying primary gallbladder carcinoma is entirely negligible [cite: 2768]

findings.description: Asymptomatic dilation of the extrahepatic common bile duct or common hepatic duct system.
features: Must be measured strictly in the short-axis plane to prevent artificial exaggeration caused by oblique imaging angles [cite: 2797]
In patients with an intact gallbladder under 60 years old, defined as a short-axis diameter greater than 6 mm [cite: 2798]
In patients post-cholecystectomy (gallbladder absent), defined as a short-axis diameter greater than 10 mm [cite: 2798]
A short-axis diameter greater than 7 mm strongly suggests true underlying bile duct obstruction if the gallbladder is intact [cite: 2799]
